content:
Electromagnetic Aerospace flying saucer- China patent

#ufotwitter

Patent describes a vehicle composed of three distinct metallic shell layers: an inner shell, an outer shell, and a top cover (half-shell). These layers are insulated from each other and constructed from multiple metallic electrode plates.

Key structural and functional components include:

Central Architecture: A cockpit is mounted on top, and insulating landing legs are attached to the bottom of the outer shell. The three shells and the cockpit are connected via an insulating central tube.

Propulsion Mechanism: The core of the propulsion system relies on high-voltage generators installed between the shells.
Generators are positioned between the top cover and outer shell, and between the inner and outer shells.
These generators connect to the electrode plates on the corresponding shells.

Operational Principle: The patent claims that these shells form an independent "electromagnetic radiation emission unit." By emitting electromagnetic radiation energy, the craft is intended to generate reactive propulsion force.

Vertical Flight: Activating all emission units simultaneously creates upward lift.

Directional Flight: Activating specific units in any chosen direction generates lateral propulsion, allowing the craft to maneuver.

The technical classification codes provided, B64C 39/06 and B64D 27/24, categorize this under aircraft with unconventional configurations and electric power/propulsion systems, respectively.
